references.text: Lamech extends the principle of sevenfold vengeance for Cain to seventy-seven times, a direct expansion of God's word in verse 15.
God establishes the principle of retribution for bloodshed after the flood, in contrast to the special protection given to Cain.
God places a mark (תָּו) on those who mourn over Jerusalem's sins to protect them, a parallel to the mark God placed on Cain.
Jesus' blood speaks better than Abel's blood; a contrast between Cain's story and the grace and protection of the new covenant.
God's servants are sealed on their foreheads for protection, a thematic parallel to the protective mark God gave Cain.
